chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah: 'O Allah, forgive those who shaved [their heads],' twice. It was said: 'And those who trimmed [their heads]?' O Messenger of Allah. He said: 'And those who trimmed.'

key_terms.اِغْفِرْ: Forgive (imperative verb from the root gh-f-r)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْحُدَيْبِيَةِ: The day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, referring to the historical event and pilgrimage

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet pray for regarding those who shaved or trimmed their hair during Hajj?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the Prophet’s supplication during the Treaty of Al-Hudaybiyyah, emphasizing that the divine mercy extends equally to those who fully shaved (*halq*) and those who merely trimmed (*qasr*) their hair. This inclusion underscores the flexibility in Hajj rituals and the Prophet’s comprehensive intercession for all pilgrims, regardless of the degree of their sacrifice. It serves as a foundational text for the jurisprudential principle that both acts are valid and equally rewarded in the context of the Prophet’s prayer.
